title: Crossing
description: A summer photograph of a Japanese level crossing, seen from below and looking up past the crossbuck into the sky, that turns out to be built like a paper tunnel book, seen through a window cut in the page. Drag, or tilt your phone, and it comes apart behind that window into its real depth planes: the sky card stands back, the wires hang in the middle, the crossbuck and its lamps float forward, each a cut-out with the street continued behind it, throwing soft shadows on the cards behind. The lens focuses on whichever plane is under your finger. Let go and it closes back into one flat photograph.
intent: Multiple layers of an image, the physical world inside the computer. After Disney's multiplane camera (1937, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiplane_camera) and paper tunnel books (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tunnel_book): one low-angle photo cut offline into seven matted, inpainted planes that separate in z with true perspective, each scaled so that from the lens axis the stack is still exactly the photograph.

sources.author: PJH (@dokae)
sources.note: Ukyo, Kyoto; 4928x3264 original (Ricoh GR II). Plated from the curated low-angle library frame kyoto-crossing-lowangle (4000x2649; chosen over setagaya-wires-up as the steeper, about 35 degrees up, and more cobalt frame). Depth from Depth Anything V2 Small via tools/depth/depth_hr.py; planes, mattes and inpainting baked by tools/depth/bakes/crossing (labels.py, bake.py): the sky card filled from a dilated matte and outpainted a quarter past each side, every wire refitted as one catenary and redrawn at one dark colour by wires.py, running on under the old house far past the frame and behind the signal so no wire ends in open sky, hidden house and town texture and the town card's overscan margin by LaMa (tools/depth/fill.py), every card that meets the frame overscanned so the front mat never shows an edge.

sources.author: Greg Zaal (Poly Haven)
sources.note: The cumulus behind the street: the 16k equirectangular's big side-lit cumulus (lon 127-153, lat 19-37; the sun is up and to the right, as in the photo), keyed from its sky at native resolution, isolated from the rows of small cloud and horizon haze below it, its keyed rim eroded and feathered at native resolution so no pale edge or notch of sky shows, relit warm-white only on the tops that face the sun and skylight blue-grey on its shaded lobes and left flank, with a darker, flat base that thins into the sky's horizon gradient, and projected stretched upright so it towers from behind the roofs past the crossbuck, by tools/depth/bakes/crossing/cumulus.py, on a card of its own between the sky and the far houses, feathered to nothing well inside its edges. The photo's own torn cloud wisps are gone from the sky card, which is now the clear gradient alone.
